audit.whatIsWrong: Granite Shield is mentioned three times as a reason Malphite wins extended trades, but nothing says how it recharges.
audit.why: It only comes back "if Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds". Unstable Matter is a flat 5-second cooldown at every rank - the shortest cooldown in either kit - so a Zac who simply keeps pulsing W denies the recharge outright and Malphite fights the whole trade with no shield. The entry currently frames his passive as a reason Zac loses long trades; it is actually the thing Zac is best equipped in the game to switch off.
audit.corrected: Added to whys[5], spikes[2].text, early and late.
sources: champ-data/_kits/malphite.json (P "If Malphite has not been hit for a few seconds, this effect recharges")

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text and whys[6] all say Malphite's ultimate out-engages or out-scales Zac's ("a more reliable game-ender than your knock-up chain", "edging the fight to him").
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 130/115/100. Let's Bounce! is 120/105/90 - ten seconds shorter at every single rank. Whatever happens in the first fight, Zac has his ultimate back first in the second, and across a game that is a meaningful number of extra engages. The entry treats his ult as strictly better when the one hard number available says Zac cycles faster.
audit.corrected: Cooldown comparison stated in whys[4], whys[6], spikes[1].text, spikes[3].text and mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Malphite the last two stages while Zac wins 55.75% over 287 games.
audit.why: The five Skill stages through laning are right - it genuinely is a farm lane. But the entry then hands Malphite both item stages, which is where the win rate actually comes from. Zac's two scaling advantages both land exactly there: percent-max-health W against a champion who stacks health and armour, and a ten-second-shorter ultimate.
audit.corrected: Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Skill / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whys are shifted out of step with the stages they label. whys[4] (the Level 6 slot) reads "At 5 there's still no reliable kill pressure", and whys[5] (the First item slot) reads "Malphite's Unstoppable Force at 6 out-engages your R".
audit.why: Both describe the wrong stage, so the level-6 card says nothing about level 6 and the first-item card says nothing about items. A player reading the chart top to bottom gets the ultimate discussed twice and the item spike never.
audit.corrected: whys[4] now covers level 6 and whys[5] covers the first item.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of the resource asymmetry, and no cooldown given for Seismic Shard.
audit.why: Malphite is mana-constrained and pays 70-90 for Q on an 8-second flat cooldown, while every Zac ability costs a share of current health and nothing else. In a farm lane decided by who can keep pressing buttons, that is the structural difference, and it compounds with the Granite Shield point: Zac can afford to pulse W purely to deny the shield, Malphite cannot afford to trade Q for it.

The existing claim that Unstoppable Force beats Let's Bounce! mirror-for-mirror because Zac can be knocked out of his own bounces is left as written - it is the entry's own claim, it is consistent with R being a repeated-bounce channel, and I have no kit-file basis to either confirm or contradict it. The kit's needsResearch block is empty, which means unknown, not false.

Unlike the squishy matchups in this slice, the templated "W the %HP ticks" line in tradeGood is genuinely right here - Malphite is a health-and-armour stacker and is among the best targets for Unstable Matter that Zac faces. Left alone.

notes: The one thing I deliberately did NOT act on: the kit file gives Zac's E a "grounding" flag, and _missing-interactions.json builds on it to claim "Your Elastic Slingshot (E) shuts off Malphite's Unstoppable Force (R)". Elastic Slingshot does not apply Grounded. The flag looks derived from the word "ground" in the description text ("attaches his arms to the ground"), and the same artefact shows up on Malphite's own Q and E ("through the ground", "slams the ground"), neither of which grounds either. I wrote nothing based on that flag in any matchup in this slice, and the corresponding missing-interactions rows for Kled, Maokai, Locke and Master Yi should be treated as unreliable for the same reason. Malphite's R also carries a "projectile" flag; it is a dash, so do not let anything downstream claim Wind Wall blocks it. The two win[] edits are short label fields and will fail a literal +/-10% band.
